text:
owen: seeing huge scale-up failures in us-west1 this morning, spike at ~08:12 UTC — autoscaler tried to spin 0->120 GPUs but most nodes are stuck NotReady. provisioning shows instances created but kubelet never becomes Ready. anyone seeing this?

maria: yep, seeing kubelet crashloops on the new nodes. logs show failed systemd units during cloud-init, lots of image-pull timeouts and cgroup errors.

tim: infra-bot flagged a lot of API 429s around the same time (create-instance). might be quota/rate-limit + our retry storm. :rotating_light:

infra-bot: INCIDENT-1978 created: "us-west1 gpu provisioner slow init causing scale-up stall" — assigned to #eng-infra, priority P1.

sre-lead: prioritize shifting traffic to eu-west1 and bring up the dedicated hot pool as fallback. @tim start the regional failover policy, @maria investigate the init scripts and image. keep me posted.

tim: kicking off regional-failover: `rctl route update --policy regional-failover --set weight=eu-west1:70,us-west1:30` — rolling now. opened support ticket CS-8891 with cloud provider about rate limits.

maria: dug in — a recent kernel packaging change in our GPU image increases boot time; systemd times out during cloud-init which runs our nv setup. canary nodes with previous image boot fine. rolling back image on canary pool now.

owen: kubectl describe node (snippet):
```
Events:
  Normal   NodeHasSufficientMemory  2s  kubelet  Node is out of disk, memory pressure
  Warning  KubeletNotReady          10s kubelet  Kubelet stopped posting status
  Warning  FailedStart              12s kubelet  Failed to start containerd-shim: permission denied
  Warning  SystemdStartFailed       13s kubelet  start request repeated too quickly
```
lots of transient permission/cgroup messages too.

tim: cloud-support replied: they saw a short-lived API rate spike, suggested temporary quota bump and to change provisioner retries to exponential backoff with jitter to avoid retry storms.

cloud-support: Support: temporarily increased instance-create rate for project to 120/min. Recommended mitigation: add exponential backoff + jitter to provisioner, and switch to pooled batch-create endpoints instead of single-instance retries.

sre-lead: actions: 1) rollback image on all new pools (done by canary now), 2) patch provisioner to backoff/jitter (PR planned), 3) add a node-ready-latency tolerance to autoscaler (allow up to 3m transient readiness), 4) smooth routing weights to avoid thrash during partial region recovery. note: cost impact — cross-region failover and hot-pool burn will add ~$4k/day while incident active.

owen: will open PRs for backoff + metric addition. also adding alert for 'node-ready-latency > 90s' so autoscaler behavior is visible.

maria: can confirm canary rollback brought readiness back to ~90s on new nodes, workloads starting fine.

tim: routing now at eu-west1:85, us-west1:15 after smoothing. metrics stable and queue latency recovered. will keep monitoring for 30m before closing.

sre-lead: good work. please capture timeline + config diffs for postmortem. note for follow-up: evaluate reserved capacity for critical pools to avoid spike fragility.

owen: noted. opening postmortem draft and follow-up tickets. thanks all. :thumbsup:
